method: For each denomination, an ordinary-least-squares line is fit through its own reported membership points, then extended to 2035 (Catholic Church is fit through only its 2010 and 2020 points - see its own note). This is a simple straight-line extrapolation, not a demographic model: it cannot see an inflection - a schism, a policy vote, an accelerating or decelerating rate - that hasn't happened yet in the data. `confidence` on every entry reflects how clean and consistent that entry's own sourcing is, from "high" (a clean multi-point single-source series) to "low" (sparse and/or internally inconsistent). Modeled after Ryan Burge's GSS-based American-religion projections (https://gist.github.com/ryanburge/e785275206cd12584b73eb4ec9b3ad52), applied here to individual denominations' own reported membership rather than survey-tradition shares.

episcopal-church.name: Episcopal Church

points.source: The Living Church, "Facing Episcopal Church Decline."
The Living Church, "TEC's Latest Numbers: The Good News and the Bad News," livingchurch.org.

episcopal-church.fit_method: linear (ordinary least squares, all reported points)
episcopal-church.note: Only 3 data points. Child-baptism counts (a decline proxy tracked by the same source: 1990 ~56,862 to 2023 ~14,735) confirm the same steady downward shape. The Church did not report a 2024 baptized-membership topline at all, citing "parochial report confusion."

pcusa.name: Presbyterian Church (USA)

points.source: So What Faith, "PCUSA Membership: 30 Years of Decline" (2023).
So What Faith, "The PCUSA Is Missing 2.6 Million People."

pcusa.fit_method: linear (ordinary least squares, all reported points)
pcusa.note: The steepest relative decline of any body here. The straight-line fit implies near-zero membership by the late 2030s - a widely-discussed (if mechanically extreme) implication of this exact trend continuing unchanged; real decline curves usually decelerate as the steepest-declining congregations close first, so treat the 2035 figure as a lower bound on plausibility, not a real forecast.

cogic.name: Church of God in Christ
cogic.fit_method: linear (ordinary least squares, all reported points)
cogic.note: Self-reported figures (~5.2-5.5M) diverge roughly 5-6x from the independent U.S. Religion Census, which counted ~624,000 in 2010 and ~920,000 in 2020 (itself a rising count on the independent measure). This is the lowest-confidence series in the whole set, shown here per the denomination's own reporting rather than the census figures - a genuinely unresolved discrepancy, not a rounding difference.
